name: Will Wilson
bio: Trained as a mathematician and AI researcher, then built distributed databases at FoundationDB, Apple, and Google.

name: Dave Scherer
bio: Created the open source VPython library as a Carnegie Mellon sophomore. Co-founded Visual Sciences (sold in 2006, later part of Adobe) and FoundationDB (bought by Apple), where he was chief architect.

name: Robert Nishihara
statusNote: Stepped down as CEO in July 2024 when Keerti Melkote took over; now leads product strategy.
bio: Harvard math, then a Berkeley PhD under Michael Jordan. Co-created Ray in RISELab and was Anyscale's first CEO.

name: Philipp Moritz
bio: Physics at Würzburg and a Cambridge math master's, then a Berkeley CS PhD (2013 to 2019) in distributed systems and ML. Went straight from the PhD to Anyscale CTO.

name: Ion Stoica
bio: Berkeley professor with a CMU PhD after a master's in Bucharest. Co-founded Conviva and Databricks (its first CEO) before Anyscale.

name: Michael I. Jordan
bio: UC San Diego cognitive science PhD. Berkeley professor of CS and statistics, previously at MIT, and one of the most influential ML researchers.

name: Peter Morelli
bio: Salesforce R&D director, then ran Twitter's 100+ engineer platform group and joined Lyft as VP of Engineering in 2015. Attended Stanford without finishing a degree.

name: Matt Klein
bio: Duke CS and a UW master's, then 20+ years in low-level systems at Microsoft, AWS EC2, and Twitter. Created Envoy at Lyft, sat on the CNCF governing board, and chose not to commercialize Envoy.

name: Martin Conte Mac Donell
bio: Founded the Buenos Aires studio Atommica (later Jampp, sold to Affle in 2021), then joined Kicksend, which Lyft acquired in 2014. Nine years at Lyft running security, privacy, and infrastructure engineering alongside Morelli and Klein.

name: Dan Lorenc
bio: MIT mechanical engineering, then Microsoft and Google (2012 to 2021). Created Minikube and helped found Sigstore, Tekton, and SLSA.

name: Matt Moore
bio: CMU CS, Microsoft from 2005, then Google, where he led container tooling (gcr.io, Cloud Run) and co-created the distroless image. VMware senior engineer and Knative steering member before Chainguard.

name: Kim Lewandowski
bio: Started in security at Lawrence Livermore Lab and founded the pet-sitting marketplace Spotwag (sold to Rover). Google PM from 2014 who created SLSA and co-created Tekton.

name: Ville Aikas
bio: UW computer engineering, then Google from 2007 as the first engineer on Kubernetes and a Knative lead. Senior staff engineer at VMware before Chainguard.

name: Scott Nichols
bio: Started on Chrome, moved to Google Cloud to build the Kubernetes Service Catalog, then VMware.

name: Nick Schrock
role: Founder; CEO, now CTO and chairman
statusNote: Handed the CEO role to Pete Hunt in November 2022 and moved to CTO and chairman.
bio: Michigan computer engineering, Microsoft, then 8 years at Facebook, where he co-created GraphQL and founded Product Infrastructure.

name: Tristan Handy
statusNote: President of Fivetran + dbt Labs since the June 2026 merger; George Fraser is CEO.
bio: Finance and IT degree, 5 years at Deloitte Consulting, a UNC MBA, then startup operations roles before founding Fishtown Analytics.

name: Drew Banin
statusNote: Stepped back from the Chief Product Officer role; still works with the dbt open source community.
bio: Worked part-time at RJMetrics to pay for Drexel, then joined Handy instead of a post-grad job and wrote the first dbt prototype.

name: Connor McArthur
bio: Engineer and engineering manager at RJMetrics and Stitch, and dbt's first CTO.

name: David Crawshaw
bio: Sydney math grad. Google staff engineer on Go and Fuchsia, then Tailscale co-founder and CTO (2019 to 2024).

name: Josh Bleecher Snyder
bio: Early AdMob engineer. Co-founded card.io (sold to PayPal in 2012) and Canopy Climate, then an early Tailscale engineer and Go contributor.

name: Kashish Gupta
bio: Penn alum (Wharton economics plus a robotics master's). A Bessemer VC who turned down a return offer to build a travel Slackbot.

name: Tejas Manohar
bio: Self-taught and skipped college. Moved to SF at 16 to be one of Segment's first 10 engineers.

name: Josh Curl
bio: One of Rancher Labs' first 10 engineers, then Segment's Personas team. Briefly co-founded Deviceplane.

name: Søren Bramer Schmidt
statusNote: Started as CTO and took over as CEO.
bio: Nearly 7 years as a developer and architect at Trustpilot. Co-founded the nutrition startup Eat Better before Prisma.

name: Johannes Schickling
statusNote: Left Prisma; later built Overtone and LiveStore.
bio: Built the VR startup Optonaut and went through Entrepreneur First in London before co-founding Graphcool.

name: Quinn Slack
statusNote: Now CEO of Amp Inc., the spinout; remains on Sourcegraph's board. Dan Adler is Sourcegraph CEO.
bio: Bleacher Report's first engineer right out of high school, then Stanford CS and Palantir. Co-founded Blend before Sourcegraph.

name: Beyang Liu
statusNote: Co-founded Amp Inc. with Slack; remains on Sourcegraph's board.
bio: Stanford CS with Stanford AI Lab research. Worked at Google and Palantir before co-founding Sourcegraph at about 24.

name: Maxim Fateev
statusNote: Swapped roles with Abbas in April 2024.
bio: Physics in Moscow, a CS master's in Rio. Led what became AWS SQS and Simple Workflow, then Google and Uber, where he co-created Cadence.

name: Samar Abbas
statusNote: Swapped roles with Fateev in April 2024.
bio: From Karachi. Microsoft from 2000, AWS Simple Workflow, then Azure's Durable Task Framework, and co-created Cadence at Uber.

name: Joran Dirk Greef
bio: Self-taught coder from Cape Town who gave up an engineering scholarship to study accounting at UCT. Wrote Node.js libraries under Ronomon, then built TigerBeetle inside Coil and spun it out in 2022.

name: Eli Schleifer
bio: Columbia visual arts and CS. Microsoft, then co-founded Directr (sold to Google in 2014), YouTube, and ran Autonomy Systems at Uber ATG.

name: David Apirian
bio: Engineer at Bloomberg and BitTorrent, then Head of Autonomy Systems and Simulation at Uber ATG.

name: Matt Matheson
bio: Developer at Microsoft, then tech lead manager at Uber ATG. Trunk's CTO.

name: Chris Clearwater
bio: Senior autonomy engineer at Uber ATG.

name: Peter Edge
bio: CMU CS and math, then about five years at Uber in Toronto, where he watched every team rebuild the same schema tooling.

name: Mitchell Hashimoto
role: Co-founder; CEO, then CTO, then engineer
statusNote: Left HashiCorp in December 2023; built the Ghostty terminal, joined Vercel's board in March 2026, and started Superlogical in July 2026.
bio: Self-taught at 12. Built Vagrant in his UW dorm, was Kiip's first engineer, and started HashiCorp at about 22.

name: Armon Dadgar
statusNote: Stayed CTO through the IBM acquisition.
bio: Started college at 16. UW CS, distributed systems architect at Kiip, then HashiCorp co-founder and CTO.

name: Will Bryk
bio: Harvard CS and physics, where he led the robotics club. Early engineer at Cresta before co-founding Exa with his roommate.

name: Jeff Wang
bio: Harvard CS and philosophy, where he ran a GPU cluster in his dorm. Three years building data infrastructure at Plaid.

name: Alexander Gallego
bio: Moved from Colombia at 14. NYU CS, FactSet and YieldMo, then co-founded Concord (sold to Akamai in 2016) and became a principal engineer there.

name: Sean Thorne
statusNote: Stepped back from daily leadership in August 2025; on the board and now founding AgentScore. Ben Eisenberg is CEO.
bio: University of Oregon. Traced the idea to a 2012 marketing class and ran sales while Nevue built the product.

name: Henry Nevue
statusNote: Stepped back from daily leadership in August 2025.
bio: Built People Data Labs' product while Thorne ran sales. Few public details on his earlier career.

name: Bobby DeSimone
bio: Teen hacker turned founder. Sold Surelock to BeyondTrust and spent 7 years there before writing Pomerium's first code.

name: John Ackerly
bio: Williams, Rhodes Scholar, Harvard MBA. White House tech policy advisor during 9/11, then a private equity investor.

name: Will Ackerly
bio: 8 to 9 years at the NSA in cloud security, where he created the Trusted Data Format that Virtru is built on.

name: Krishna Gade
bio: Minnesota CS master's. Microsoft and Bing, Twitter, Pinterest, then Facebook, where his team built "Why am I seeing this post?"

name: Amit Paka
bio: Product roles at Microsoft, Expedia, and PayPal. Sold Flockish and Parable (to Samsung) before co-founding Fiddler.

name: Henry Ward
bio: Michigan math and CS plus a finance master's. Software and sales engineering roles, then founded Secondsight before eShares.

name: Manu Kumar
bio: Serial seed investor (K9 Ventures) who co-founded eShares with Ward and became chairman.

name: Peter Zhou
bio: Yale CS with stints at Facebook and Atrium. Pivoted through failed ideas before Rutter (YC S19).

name: Eric Yu
bio: Co-founded Rutter with Zhou. Few public details on his earlier career.

name: Jeremy Tsui
statusNote: Joined Concord as Managing Director, Capital Markets after the March 2026 acquisition.
bio: Debt investor in Goldman Sachs' Merchant Banking Division, where he saw borrowers struggle with credit agreements.

name: Josiah Tsui
bio: Worked at Palantir and Ironclad (another Haystack company) before co-founding Finley with his brother.

name: Kevin Suh
bio: First engineer at Nova Credit before co-founding Finley.

name: Kwindla Hultman Kramer
bio: Founding CTO of AllAfrica, then co-founder and CEO of Oblong Industries from 2005 to 2013. Holds a Harvard AB and an MIT Media Lab MS, and started the Pipecat open source project at Daily.

name: Nina Kuruvilla
bio: Co-founder of Daily since January 2016 with a Harvard philosophy degree. Her public record before Daily is sparse.

name: Doug Brunton
statusNote: Left in 2017 and held a board seat until 2019; VP Engineering at Plectica, then Frameable since 2021.
bio: Founding partner of Plus Three, which took the Democratic National Committee's fundraising online, then an engineer at Shutterstock and Oblong Industries. Co-founded Daily (then Pluot Communications) in 2015 and built its early hardware prototypes.

name: Jon Dahl
bio: Co-founded Zencoder in 2010 and sold it to Brightcove in 2012, then served as Brightcove VP of Technology. Studied philosophy at Wheaton and theology at Trinity before turning to programming.

name: Steve Heffernan
role: Co-founder; Head of Product 2015 to 2021, now Product Architect
statusNote: Stepped back from Head of Product in July 2021 and remains as co-founder and product architect, still shipping Video.js and Mux work in 2026.
bio: Created Video.js in 2010 alongside Zencoder, which he co-founded and sold to Brightcove in 2012, then led open player technology at Brightcove. Holds a BS and an MBA from Azusa Pacific.

name: Matthew McClure
bio: Developer evangelist and engineer on Brightcove's Zencoder and Video.js teams before co-founding Mux in 2015. Organizes the Demuxed conference for video engineers.

name: Adam Brown
role: Co-founder, Head of Technology and Architecture
bio: Built cloud transcoding on Brightcove's Zencoder team and VR cloud rendering at Otoy before co-founding Mux. Leads technology and architecture at Mux.

name: Yadhu Gopalan
bio: Spent 19 years at Microsoft on Windows CE and Windows Phone, then five at Amazon building back-end systems for Fire OS, Amazon Go, and AWS, and holds 35 patents in embedded systems and security. Co-founded Esper in 2017 and has been its CEO since.

name: Shiv Sundar
role: Co-founder; COO, now Chief Business Operator
statusNote: Esper's leadership page now lists him as Co-Founder and Chief Business Operator, with David Barclay as COO.
bio: Program manager for Windows Phone partnerships at Microsoft, then product and partnerships roles at Samsung, Quixey, Cyanogen, and Huawei, where he ran global Android strategy. Co-founded Esper in 2017, launched its India operations, and leads revenue and go-to-market.

name: Fred Schott
role: Founder; Astro Project Steward until Aug 2026
statusNote: Sold the company to Cloudflare in January 2026 and handed the Astro Project Steward role to Matthew Phillips in August 2026; his Cloudflare title is not stated publicly.
bio: Studied computer science at Tufts, then worked at Box, WorkLife, and Google's Polymer team on Web Components tooling. Created the Snowpack build tool, formed The Astro Technology Company around the Astro framework, and sold it to Cloudflare in January 2026.

name: Matthew Phillips
role: Co-creator of Astro; Project Steward since Aug 2026
statusNote: Moved to Cloudflare with the January 2026 acquisition and became Astro's Project Steward in August 2026, taking over from Schott.
bio: Louisville-based front-end engineer who spent years as a full-time open source maintainer of CanJS and StealJS at the consultancy Bitovi and wrote the Haunted web components library. Joined Fred Schott's Skypack as an engineer, co-created Astro, and now stewards the project at Cloudflare.

name: Ramiro Berrelleza
bio: Grew up in Guadalajara, Mexico, and spent his career on cloud services and developer tools as a software engineer on Microsoft Azure, an early engineer at ElasticBox, and an architect at Atlassian. Co-founded Okteto in 2018 and led it through Y Combinator's W19 batch as CEO.

name: Pablo Chico de Guzmán
bio: Earned a 2012 doctorate in logic programming at the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the IMDEA Software Institute before building Docker Cloud, the container platform formerly known as Tutum. Co-founded Okteto in 2018 as CTO and leads the Docker Madrid meetup as a Docker Community Leader.

name: Ramón Lamana
bio: Front-end engineer who built developer tools at eyeOS and ElasticBox, then worked at Google on consumer products including Inbox by Gmail and YouTube. Co-founded Okteto in 2018 and leads product.

name: Yevgeny Pats
statusNote: CloudQuery merged into env zero in March 2026 and Pats became CTO of the combined company.
bio: Began as an R&D software engineer in an Israel Defense Forces cyber intelligence unit, then joined an enterprise security startup that Check Point acquired. Founded the continuous fuzzing service Fuzzit, sold it to GitLab in 2020, and started CloudQuery as an open source project in 2021.

name: Ivan Tsarynny
bio: Co-founded the Toronto employee-advocacy startup PostBeyond in 2013 and led it as CEO through a 2016 Series A; Influitive acquired it in 2021. Leads an OWASP Top 10 project, sits on the Standards Council of Canada GDPR committee, and testified before the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission in 2024.

name: Vitaliy Lim
bio: Engineer and security researcher since the early 2000s who holds a master's degree in electrical and computer engineering. Founded PostBeyond in 2013, later acquired by Influitive, and co-founded Feroot in 2017 as CTO.

name: Frederic Branczyk
statusNote: Dash0 acquired Polar Signals in August 2026; Branczyk is now VP of Data Engineering at Dash0.
bio: Prometheus and Thanos maintainer who led observability engineering at CoreOS and then at Red Hat as senior principal engineer, and served four years as tech lead of Kubernetes SIG Instrumentation. Founded Polar Signals in Berlin at the end of 2020 and open sourced the Parca continuous profiler in 2021.

name: Michael Callahan
statusNote: Handed the CEO role to Rahul Kashyap in July 2018 and moved to a technical role and board seat; Awake was sold to Arista in October 2020. He remains a Datadog director (on that board since 2011).
bio: Harvard social studies graduate and Rhodes Scholar who was a junior research fellow in mathematics at Oxford before co-founding PolyServe, a storage software company sold to HP in 2007. Incubated Awake Security as a Greylock entrepreneur in residence and was its founding CEO from August 2014 to July 2018.

name: Keith Amidon
statusNote: Awake was sold to Arista Networks in October 2020; his current role is not confirmed on any page that loaded.
bio: Co-founder of IntruVert Networks, an intrusion detection company acquired by McAfee, then an engineering director at Nicira and VMware in software-defined networking and a co-author of the Open vSwitch paper. Joined Awake's founding team in 2014 to lead high performance network processing.

name: Debabrata Dash
statusNote: Awake was sold to Arista Networks in October 2020; his later role at Arista could not be confirmed from a page that loaded.
bio: IIT Kanpur engineer who was a senior software architect at ArcSight, returned to Carnegie Mellon for a databases PhD, and became a distinguished technologist at HP after it bought ArcSight. Led engineering at CipherCloud before co-founding Awake Security in 2014 to run its analytics pipeline.

name: Gary Golomb
statusNote: Awake was sold to Arista in October 2020; he is now Chief Research Officer at Quantum Offense, a quantum computing threat research venture.
bio: Former Marine Force Recon who moved into intrusion detection research at Enterasys and forensics at George Washington University, founded Proventsure (acquired by NetWitness, later RSA), and was among the first employees at Cylance. Co-founded Awake Security in 2014 as its chief research officer and lead threat investigator.

name: Zack Kanter
bio: Started an auto parts business at 16 that became Proforged, ran it bootstrapped for more than a decade, and sold it to Drake Automotive Group, a Huron Capital portfolio company, in 2018. Founded Stedi in 2017 as a sole founder and remains its CEO.

name: Gavin Uhma
statusNote: Cape's 2026 About page lists him as co-founder and board member without the CTO title he held through at least 2021.
bio: Was CTO of Slightly Social and then co-founded GoInstant, a Halifax browser collaboration startup sold to Salesforce for about $70 million in 2012. After a stint at Salesforce and the Sidestory app, he co-founded Cape Privacy in 2018 as CTO and is also an angel investor.

name: Ben DeCoste
bio: GoInstant alum who was CTO of the Halifax storytelling app Sidestory alongside Gavin Uhma before the group regrouped in 2018 to start Cape Privacy. Co-authored the 2018 TF Encrypted paper on private machine learning in TensorFlow and still writes for Cape's engineering blog in 2026.

name: Ian Livingstone
statusNote: Left Cape Privacy in summer 2020, according to Entrevestor's April 2021 report.
bio: Dalhousie graduate who joined GoInstant straight out of school in 2011, led a 25-person engineering team at Salesforce after the acquisition, and worked at Manifold with GoInstant's former CEO. Co-founded Cape Privacy in 2018 and left in 2020.

name: Idit Levine
bio: Former professional basketball player in Israel who taught herself to code, studied computer science and biology at Bar-Ilan, and built cloud infrastructure at DynamicOps, CloudSwitch, and Intigua before becoming CTO of EMC's cloud management division, where she created the open source UniK unikernel platform. Founded Solo.io in Boston in 2017 as a sole founder and still runs it.
